reviews.text: Brilliantly addictive and yet frustratingly challenging is the best way to describe this wonderful entry into the side scrolling platformer genre going toe to toe against titans like Dead Cells and Dead Cells DLCs. Raiting-wise it would be like this: Artstyle: 9/10 Combat: 7/10 Exploration: 10/10 Eyeballs: 1/2 Soundtrack: 6/10 My short 4 minute video review can be seen right here: https://youtu.be/19QeGSZIRIk

So, I like Ants Took My Eyeball. I liked it when I took a look at the early demo a couple years ago, and I like it even more now. I recorded some of my progress in Ants Took My Eyeball. [b]Please take a look if you value a more Audio / Visual experience, as I discuss the game in detail as I Double Jump, Dash, Hack and Blast my way through it; in some semblance of style perhaps![/b] https://youtu.be/3aIgKEstNxM Ants Took My Eyeball is an Indie, 2D Action Roguelike Sidescroller with Pixel Graphics and Procedural Generation. It feels a bit like Caveblazers, + guns; fun! It’s a 2D Platformer with awesome loot, melee weapons, gadgets and guns to find, and packing PermaDeath to keep the intensity flowing. With up to 4 player local co-op multiplayer! Awesome! [h1]RPG Stuff![/h1] You’ll find gold, trinkets, gadgets, and ammo in the random dungeons, feeding both your character’s shopping needs and your guns, letting you build up your character with both the gear you find, and the gear you fancy at the shops. Gold is the within run progression, used at between lvls at the shop to buy new trinkets, gadgets, melee and ranged weapons, and ammo; fun. [b]The Trinkets![/b] Many of the trinkets are powerful: think an additional jump, another dash, or the Bloody Mandible, Which grants 2 seconds of 30% increased damage & 20% increased movement speed on making a kill, great for your bug killing sprees! Or the Lead Charm, which makes your hits apply a 1 second 40% speed debuff; handy! These kinds of trinkets shape a run, and change how you approach the random dungeon lvls; and combined with the different kinds of melee weapons, the guns, and the gadgets, you have an Action Roguelike that feels great to play, and provides plenty of options to help keep the gameplay and combat fresh. [h1]The World, and Exploration![/h1] Healing is rare in the dungeon, so try not to get hit! You do get healed at the start of each shop you reach, like in Noita; handy, just gotta make it to the portal… Coins disappear after a bit, as do bullets! Beware! There are thorn gates where you have to dash through them or take 1 hp bump damage; ok. There are canopic jars that grant gems and gold, but they also revive all killed enemies in the area, bringing them back as ghosts, presenting an interesting gameplay choice for the player, so make certain it is worth it! Spikes are present too, both on the floors and the ceilings, but they break on dealing damage and you can break them with a whack; so no Spelunky style instant kill spike pits here! [b]So Much Mobility![/b] Right at the start, you have a double jump and an air dash, so you start with massive mobility, making it pretty easy to quickly get around and avoid hits, which is a good idea, as to heal, you have to make it to the next shop a floor down. Plus, you can wall jump all the way up if you have a flat vertical wall; nice. Wall clinging / sliding are is too, and remember: you can smash spikes to prevent them from impaling you if you fall. [h1]Hack and Blast Combat:[/h1] Right off the bat: there is no default bump damage present; good! Enemies have to make an attack animation to hurt you usually; unless they got some kind of flame or frost aura, which is fair. You are strong here, right at the start. There is no stamina system present here either: so jump, dash, & swing away! Your melee attacks hit hard, and have both a stagger, plus a significant knockback on most enemies; helping to make the player feel powerful, right at the start; good. Some of the guns are full auto, and some are semi-automatic, so you have meaningful ranged options. Your ranged attacks have a bit of stagger too, with a bit of knockback; serving to differentiate them from melee; good. Your guns are fuelled by bullets, chemo ammo, and batteries, depending on what they are. SMGs, revolvers, and needle guns use bullets, the acid and flamethrower use chem rounds, while the laser guns use batteries, as expected. There are also the Gadgets. Gadgets recharge off of kills. From the humble rock, addictive and performance enhancing coffee, to explosive potions, they can be a powerful additional supplement to your more conventional hack and blast options. [h1]Meta Progression:[/h1] Meta Progression in Ants Took My Eyeball is present in the form of gems found in chests, which are use to unlock appliances in bug buddy’s lair to grant you bonuses: think +15 starting hp, coffee that will drop in lvls for bonuses, a money tree you can find in the lvls to get more gold, minor, but impactful stuff like that. Controller Support is present, and good, as is good old Mouse & Keyboard, in case that is your preference. I went mostly with the gamepad here, as 2d side-scrollers often feel better with a controller in hand. [h1]Local Co-Op:[/h1] To enable, just have player 2 hit a button while in the intro bug area before you jump down. Note: it does not work if you try to join when not at the start. Remember: Player 2 is teleported to player 1 if they get off the screen in about 4 seconds, so Player 2 should stick with #1. While I do like Ants Took My Eyeball, I did come across some areas where I feel it could be even better. Please let me know if anyone thinks any of this is off-base. I will try and keep this organized. [b]Suggestions:[/b] [h1]1: My Money![/h1] Coins do disappear after a bit, as do bullets! It really hurts to lose out on the drops. I understand it is to add some additional pressure and forward momentum to the game, but does that applied pressure add enough to balance out the induced player pain? I say no, and the game would feel better if money and ammo didn’t just magically poof away after a few seconds. If there was say, a magical teleporting / tunneling thief (perhaps an ant) that poofed in, and snatched them up though, that would be interesting, as there could be an opportunity to catch them, waste em, or drive em off. It also presents the possibility of tracking them down there to their lair later and reclaiming all your stolen gold… [h1]2: Boo![/h1] Am I a Ghost? It feels like it, as there is no monster collision or slowdown when I literally walk right through them! A 50% speed reduction when you try to run through monsters would feel nice here, representing the players ducking and weaving through their space on their way by. That would help cut down on the “Boo” factor here. It would also make the monsters more threatening to the player, as you will no longer be able to just walk through them at full speed; you have to play a bit of a speed price for it, giving the monster a chance to take a bite! [h1]3: Rebindable keys Planned?[/h1] [h1]4: Minor Bug: Game Crashed at least 2 times while Recording After a Run.[/h1] Nothing was lost, as the crash occurred after I died, but still, there were minor crashes, so I have to mention them. Note: This is the initial launch version of Ants Took My Eyeball and thus any encountered bugs or other oddness is not representative of the final product. Still, Ants Took My Eyeball is offering an intense Action Side-scroller with Perma Death + local coop that looks, feels, and sounds great. Watch?

This is an okay game, teetering on the edge of being a good game, with the potential to become a great game. Let me explain: the fundamentals of Ants Took My Eyeball are quite polished. The controls feels responsive, the art is gorgeous, and the sound design is impactful. Moving and shooting simply feel good, which makes the moment-to-moment gameplay fluid and fun. The game falls short in a couple of areas, though. While there are a decent amount of weapons, a lot of them don't feel particularly different from one another. Ranged weapons are more distinct, but melee weapons feel a bit homogeneous, and a lot (but not all) of the gadgets boil down to "throw this thing in an arc". The level generation is also not great. ATME clearly takes a lot of inspiration from Caveblazers, opting to create broad, open levels to explore. However, the procedural generation of ATME lacks the wacky verticality and destructible environments of Caveblazers, resulting in levels that don't feel particularly different from another. There's a notable lack of platforming despite the player movement tools (double jump, wall cling) that exist, and, after just two runs, you'll be able to glean how the game creates special map nodes, which saps a lot of the mystery from the levels. This all results in levels feeling quite stale. Notice a through-line between the criticisms in the previous paragraph? There's a lack of elements that contribute to run-to-run variety, and that is NOT good for a roguelite. However, I believe this can be fixed. Balancing tweaks to weapons and gadgets, plus additional special tilesets for levels, can be developed to improve run variety. The game also DESPERATELY needs a perk/class system like Caveblazers as a sort of 'manual override' to guarantee some freshness between runs; adding such a system would be a marked improvement for the game. Additionally, the in-run crafting system, while basic, has potential, and expanding on that to make it less linear would open up more buildcrafting playspace. However, those things don't exist right now, and we're left with a game that feels pretty good to play, but gets stale quickly. Is ATME a bad game? No. But I can't shake this nagging feeling that ATME is just Caveblazers But Worse. The art direction and tone of ATME is interesting, but that's really the only interesting thing about it. It doesn't introduce any fresh mechanics or systems to the genre, and what mechanics & systems it does have have been executed better by other games. Caveblazers, Vagante, and Risk of Rain Returns are all games that hit the same notes as ATME, but are better AND cheaper. In a world where those games exist, I just can't recommend ATME. It simply has nothing to make it worth playing over those other games. However, I WILL be checking back in on ATME in the future. If post-launch support continues, and the developers work on adding more dynamism and variety to runs, I could see ATME being a much better game a year or so down the line. The fundamentals ARE good, which, in some ways, is the hardest (and most important) aspect to nail down. I think it's only up from here, so, if you're interested, keep your eye (pun intended) on this game.

Not terrible, not great. Plays like an average action rogue-lite, but it doesn't do anything new or interesting. The options for Melee and ranged Weapons are neat, but throwing away your current weapon is way to prominent. It's hard to tell if you got hit and your health bar is pretty small. The moment-to-moment gameplay doesn't make me feel smart for planing a good attack or powerful for beating lots of enemies. The level generations works, but doesn't look like anything. It's all just... meh. Maybe there is more interesting stuff to find than trinkets that give 5% to whatever, but I'm not going to grind some meta progression.

It's not a "NO", more like "Not recommended in its current state." They might be able to add in the necessary things to make this a pretty good roguelike/roguelite. My issues with the game: - It's a platformer but there's nothing like platform challenge rooms? Movement feels good but the game doesn't really do anything interesting with it. - Combat is too slow and unresponsive in my opinion. Why does the dodge even have a delay? Not talking about the cooldown, that's fine, but you hit the dodge button and only after a small delay will you actually go through with it. - Come on man... a water level? Slowing movement and combat down even more is not a good thing for this game. Maybe I missed an item that could've made it bearable though. - Sometimes Elite enemies will spawn and they'll have some buffs that make them more difficult to fight, they're fine for the most part, my only gripe is with the electric one. You hit it and it'll drop a floating electric orb that damages you every now and again when you're in its area of effect, in most areas fighting it is just a drag. Wouldn't it have been better to have the orb only shoot lightning if you have been hit by something else WHILE you're in the area of effect? - Finally the most glaring issue... it's a rogue but there's no alternate paths/regions? Only 1 character? The bosses are always the same. Most of the weapons feel like reskins of eachother. The trinkets don't feel like they actually have any real impact on gameplay except maybe the "adds another jump" trinket. Fast paced combat... Why not play Dead Cells, Nuclear Throne or Hades? Lots of items and on-screen mayhem... Why not play Nuclear Throne, Risk of Rain 1 or 2? Great weapon variety and fun boss fights... Why not play Enter the Gungeon or Dungreed? Good platforming and some fun RPG mechanics... Why not play Vagante? It's more expensive than most other rogues but at the same time seems to have less content. In the 8 hours I've played I only completed one run and I've seen many of the same weapons/trinkets pop up, that leads me to believe that what I've seen is all there is to see. I've never played a rogue before this that made me feel like 1 finished run was really all I needed. Bosmic Forge has done really well for their first game! But if I have to judge it as a rogue then I find it lacking.
